statement: Four bus stops lie on a straight street in the order P, Q, R, S. From P to R is 700 m, from Q to S is 900 m, and from P to S is 1200 m. How far is it from Q to R?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the two shorter distances, 900 minus 700, without drawing where they sit on the street.
I worked out 1200 minus 900, which is the distance from P to Q, not from Q to R.
I worked out 1200 minus 700, which is the distance from R to S, not from Q to R.
I added 700 and 900 and did not notice that the stretch from Q to R is counted inside both of them.

hints: Draw the street as a line and mark the four stops.
Write each given distance above your line as an arc. Look for a piece of street that is covered twice, or a piece you can find by taking a part away from the whole street.
P to S is 1200 m and Q to S is 900 m, so P to Q is 300 m. Now use P to R.

solutions.reliable: Draw P, Q, R, S on a line. P to S is 1200 m and Q to S is 900 m, so P to Q is 1200 - 900 = 300 m. Then Q to R is P to R minus P to Q: 700 - 300 = 400 m. The transferable idea: a quick sketch with the numbers written on it turns a memory puzzle into reading off a picture.
solutions.elegant: P to R and Q to S together cover the whole street once and the middle piece Q to R twice, so 700 + 900 = 1200 + QR, which gives QR = 400 m.

whyOnTest: Drawing the diagram is the skill here: overlapping distances given in words are hard to hold in your head, and a sketch shows the overlap at once.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
